findings.title: Real-world models are early-stopped and checkpoint-selected on the test set
findings.claim: In the real-world driver, the validation dataloader passed to trainer.fit is dm.test_dataloader(); the EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint callbacks (lines 169-180) both monitor f'val_{loss}', and line 203 loads checkpoint_callback.best_model_path before trainer.test on the same test loader (line 212).
findings.concern: Early stopping and best-checkpoint selection are performed on the very set used to report Table 1/Table 2 MAE, so the reported errors are optimistically biased test-set-selected values rather than honest held-out estimates, even though a genuine 10% validation split (val_len) is configured and left unused.
findings.resolution: Re-run Table 1/2 with val_dataloaders=dm.val_dataloader() (as run_prediction.py already does for synthetic tasks) and report test MAE only for the val-selected checkpoint; confirm whether the published numbers used the test set for selection.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix B: 'We sequentially split the windows into 70%/10%/20% partitions for training, validation, and testing'; Tables 1-2
findings.reason: Quote matches exactly at lines 200-202; check_script confirms all conditions: val_dataloaders=dm.test_dataloader() in trainer.fit, EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint both monitor val_<loss>, best checkpoint loaded before test, and val_len is configured but unused in all three real-world dataset configs.

findings.title: 'Diffusion Convolution' MPTCN silently instantiates GCNConv, not DiffConv
findings.claim: DiffConvMixin (used by MPTCN_DiffConvModel = model name 'mptcn_diff', the default model in config/realworld.yaml) sets gnn_class to torch_geometric GCNConv with GCN kwargs — byte-identical to GCNMixin — so the spatial MP layer is a standard GCN; the tsl DiffConv symbol imported on line 3 is never used anywhere in the repo.
findings.concern: The paper's real-world MPTCN (Tables 1-2) is described as using the Diffusion Convolution (DCNN) operator with messages 'from both incoming and outgoing neighbors up to 2 hops', but the code runs a single-hop symmetric GCN, so the reported 'MPTCN (DCNN)' numbers correspond to a different, undirected 1-hop operator than described.
findings.resolution: Set DiffConvMixin.gnn_class = DiffConv (with its k-hop / bidirectional kwargs) and re-run, or correct the paper to state that GCNConv was used; confirm which operator produced Tables 1-2.
findings.paper_ref: Section 5.1: 'the Diffusion Convolution (DCNN) operator [54] as the MP layer'; Appendix B: 'messages with different weights from both incoming and outgoing neighbors up to 2 hops'
findings.reason: Quote matches exactly at lines 26-33; check_script confirms DiffConvMixin.gnn_class=GCNConv (identical to GCNMixin), DiffConv is referenced only in the import line (gnn_mixin.py:3) and never instantiated anywhere, and realworld.yaml defaults to model mptcn_diff.

findings.title: No code for Table 2 (FOSR rewiring and RGCN combined-rewiring experiment)
findings.quote: We adopt FOSR [56] as the graph rewiring method
findings.claim: Table 2 reports EngRAD MAE for the 'original graph' vs 'FOSR rewiring' with an RGCN and a DCNN message-passing layer, but the repo contains no FOSR rewiring, no RGCN layer, and no rewiring machinery (grep for fosr/rgcn/rewir/relational returns 0 hits), and no config selects such an experiment.
findings.concern: The paper's combined spatial+temporal rewiring result — used to argue temporal rewiring contributes the largest marginal gain — cannot be reproduced from the provided code.
findings.resolution: Release the FOSR rewiring code, the RGCN model, and the Table 2 run config (or point to where they live).
findings.paper_ref: Table 2 and Section 5.1 'Combining spatial and temporal rewiring'
findings.reason: Paper quote located at paper_text.txt line 846; check_script confirms 0 hits for fosr, rgcn, rewir, relational, first_order_spectral, RelConv, and RGCNConv across all .py, .yaml, and .md files in the repo.

findings.title: No code reproduces Table 5 (TemporalTreeNeighboursMatch accuracy)
findings.quote: the topology is a tree and is fixed, while the nonzero leaf features are placed either at the initial
findings.claim: Appendix D / Table 5 reports test accuracy on a fixed-tree TemporalTreeNeighboursMatch classification task, but the repo has no tree graph generator (generators are identity/ring/crossed_ring/path/lollipop/<k>_reg/<n>_barbell/community) and no classification machinery (grep for tree/neighboursmatch/accuracy/cross_entropy/argmax returns 0 hits; losses/metrics are regression MSE/MAE).
findings.concern: The appendix task and its Table 5 accuracies are not reproducible from the released code, contradicting the checklist claim that code to reproduce the experiments is available.
findings.resolution: Add the tree generator, the classification head/loss, and the accuracy metric used for Table 5, plus a run config.
findings.reason: Paper quote located at paper_text.txt line 2195; check_script confirms tree is absent from the eight available graph generators (barbell/community/crossed_ring/identity/lollipop/path/reg/ring) and 0 hits for tree, neighboursmatch, accuracy, cross_entropy, crossentropy, argmax, NLLLoss across the entire repo.

findings.title: No dedicated config/driver to reproduce ROCKETMAN (Fig 4 / Fig 7)
findings.quote: Figure 4: Success rate (%) of TTS MPTCNs on the ROCKETMAN dataset, where the goal is to copy
findings.claim: The repo ships configs only for the copy-time plot (run_copy_time.yaml) and the real-world tables; there is no config sweeping graph type (ring/lollipop), filter size P (2/3), spatial distance k and temporal distance i, and the memory-dataset target for memorize='neighbors' adds a source 'dump' term rather than the pure k-hop-neighbor average described for ROCKETMAN.
findings.concern: It is unclear how to reproduce Fig 4/Fig 7 from the provided configs, and whether the memory dataset's target exactly implements the ROCKETMAN label.
findings.resolution: Provide the ROCKETMAN run config(s) and confirm the exact (memorize, dump, horizon, spatial_order) settings that produce the Fig 4/7 (k, i) grid.
findings.reason: Paper quote located at paper_text.txt line 742; config listing confirms only run_copy_time.yaml (which uses identity graph with spatial_order=0, not ring/lollipop) and real-world configs exist; no sweep config targets the (graph_type, filter_size_P, spatial_k, temporal_i) parameter grid shown in Fig 4/7.
